The '''International Alliance of App-based Transport Workers''' ('''IAATW''') is a network of [[Trade union|trade unions]] organizing [[Ridesharing company|ridesharing]] and other [[Gig worker|gig]] transport workers.

==History==
IAATW was founded in January 2020 during an international conference of app-based transport trade unions hosted by the UPHD which is now branded as App Drivers & Couriers Union,<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://inequality.org/research/driven-to-organize-uber-lyft/ |title=Driven to Organize: App-Based Drivers Launch New Global Network |website=Inequality.org |publisher=[[Institute for Policy Studies]] |date=2020-02-10}}</ref> with financial support from the [[Open Society Foundations]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine |last=Vargese |first=Sanjana |date=17 February 2020 |title=Gig economy workers have a new weapon in the fight against Uber |language=en-GB |magazine=[[Wired UK]] |url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/gig-economy-uber-unions |access-date=2022-06-05 |issn=1357-0978}}</ref>

During the conference, organisers and drivers shared success stories and challenges, reflecting on the global nature of the gig economy as well as country specific challenges, like [[2020 California Proposition 22|Proposition 22 in California]].<ref name=":0" />

In July 2020, IAATW together with the [[App Drivers and Couriers Union]] and NGO [[Worker Info Exchange]] started a campaign of [[Uber BV v Aslam|supporting Uber drivers in filing legal complaints against the company]] for failing to provide access to their personal data.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.eu/article/drivers-take-legal-action-against-uber-to-demand-their-data/|title= Drivers take legal action against Uber to demand their data|author=Laura Kayali|website=[[Politico]]|date=2020-06-20}}</ref>

In ''[[Uber BV v Aslam]]'' [2021] UKSC 5, the UK Supreme Court ruled in favour of IAATW-affiliated members App Drivers & Couriers Union<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.adcu.org.uk/news-posts/supreme-court-landmark-victory-over-uber |title=The United Kingdom Supreme Court today handed an emphatic victory to Uber drivers in their six-year battle for worker rights including the right to earn the minimum wage and holiday pay |agency=ADCU |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311230513/https://www.adcu.org.uk/news-posts/supreme-court-landmark-victory-over-uber |archive-date=2026-03-11}}</ref> that [[Uber]] drivers should be considered as workers. Afterwards, IAATW affiliates relaunched a similar case in South Africa and considered opening one in Nigeria.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://restofworld.org/2021/gig-workers-around-the-world-are-finally-organizing/|title='We're all fighting the giant': Gig workers around the world are finally organizing|website=[[Rest of World]]|first=Peter|last=Guest|date=2021-09-21}}</ref>
